page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a member of the Lasv4 server family, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, 24 physical cores, and 2 threads per core operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 11519 GB of Premium Storage capable capacity. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in several areas, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics placing in the top 25%. The server also demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and text processing via Geekbench, alongside high-throughput Redis SET operations reaching 70.18 million operations per second. However, performance tradeoffs are visible in uncached memory bandwidth read and write operations, which fall into the average category. Additionally, while LLM inference speeds for small 135M models are strong, text generation performance for large 70B models is poor, landing in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L48as_v4 offers a high density of local storage and memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial local data caching without the overhead of external storage arrays. The hardware profile is optimized for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive applications, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and moderate-scale language model prompt processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a Lasv4-family server featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz, 384.0 GB of RAM, and 11519 GB of local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 system delivers strong CPU and memory performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores placing in the top 25%. It excels at Redis operations, reaching 70.18 million operations per second, and multi-threaded decompression. However, uncached memory bandwidth remains average, and large-scale LLM text generation is a notable performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10%. Given its high storage capacity and 8.0 GB of RAM per core, this server is highly efficient for storage-heavy databases, memory-intensive applications, and software compilation workloads.
